Rice.pres: Store in hermetic silos or multi-layer sealed bags. Keep moisture below 12%. Aerate periodically to purge moisture hotspots.
Rice.insects: Rice Weevil (Sitophilus oryzae), Lesser Grain Borer

Wheat.pres: Hermetic silo or flat dry warehouse. Pre-clean to remove broken grains and chaff; ensure grain moisture < 11.5%.
Wheat.insects: Granary Weevil (Sitophilus granarius), Sawtoothed Grain Beetle

Maize.pres: Forced-air drying to 13% moisture immediately after harvest. Aerated steel bins to prevent dangerous aflatoxin spikes.

Cotton.pres: Baled lint stored on raised wooden dunnage with fire sprinklers and strict humidity control to prevent fiber mildew.
Cotton.insects: Pink Bollworm residual, Warehouse Carpet Beetle

Sugarcane.pres: Crush within 24–48 hours of harvest. In transit storage, mist stalks and shade to halt sucrose inversion into reducing sugars.

Linseed.pres: Dry to 7–9% moisture. Aerate silo continuously during the first 30 days to dissipate respiration heat and prevent rancidity.
Linseed.insects: Rust-Red Flour Beetle, Sawtoothed Grain Beetle

Olive.pres: Shallow ventilated plastic lugs (max 20 kg per lug) to prevent fruit crushing. Cold press within 24–48 hours.

Oil Palm.pres: Process Fresh Fruit Bunches (FFB) within 24 hours. Bruised fruits trigger rapid enzymatic lipase breakdown of free fatty acids.

Pigeon Pea.pres: Sun dry to 9–10% moisture. Store in hermetic multi-layer PICS bags or sealed galvanized bins to suffocate pulse beetles.

Cowpea.pres: Solar heating on black plastic sheets before bagging to destroy internal bruchid larvae; seal in airtight hermetic bags.

Moth Bean.pres: Clean and dry to <9% moisture. Store in moisture-proof drums or hermetic bins away from heat sources.

Faba Bean.pres: Thorough drying to 11% moisture. Avoid high storage temperatures which cause rapid seed coat tanning and hardening.

Clover.pres: Dehumidified cold seed room. Pack in foil-laminated moisture-proof bags to sustain high germination vigor.

Bermuda Grass.pres: Clean, de-hull, and dry seeds to 8–10% moisture. Store in hermetic multi-wall kraft bags in dry godowns.

Timothy Grass.pres: Air-dry in shaded ventilated racks; seal in airtight drums with silica gel to preserve seed viability.

Fescue.pres: Maintain low temperature (0–10°C) to prevent loss of beneficial symbiotic fungal endophytes (Epichloë).

Brome.pres: De-awn and screen seeds; store in breathable jute sacks with polythene liners in rodent-proof sheds.

Vetch.pres: Sun dry harvested seeds to 9% moisture; pack in airtight containers to avoid bruchid multiplication.

Sweet Potato.pres: MANDATORY: Cure at 28–30°C and 90% RH for 5–7 days to heal surface wounds before storage. NEVER store below 10°C (chilling injury causes core breakdown).
Sweet Potato.fungus: Black rot (Ceratocystis fimbriata), Rhizopus soft rot

Cassava.pres: Waxing fresh roots or packing in moist sawdust boxes prevents rapid post-harvest vascular streaking (PPD).

Yam.pres: Field cure at 32°C for 4 days. Store on slatted vertical wooden racks with continuous natural cross-ventilation. Keep above 12°C.

Turnip.pres: Remove tops leaving 1 cm neck; store unwashed in slatted plastic crates; maintain 95% humidity to prevent spongy pithiness.

Radish.pres: Hydrocool to 2°C immediately. Package in perforated polyethylene liners to retain moisture and turgidity.
Radish.fungus: Black root rot (Aphanomyces raphani), Soft rot
Radish.insects: Flea beetles residual, Root fly larvae

Shallot.pres: Field-cure tops for 2 weeks until neck tissue is completely sealed and paper-dry. Maintain low humidity (<70%) to stop root regrowth.
Shallot.fungus: Neck rot (Botrytis allii), Black mold (Aspergillus niger)

Capsicum.pres: CRITICAL: Do not store below 7°C (chilling injury causes sheet pitting and calyx rot). Wrap in micro-perforated film.

Chilli.pres: For dry chillies: sun dry to <10% moisture; store in polythene-lined gunny bags in darkness to preserve bright red carotenoids.

Squash.pres: Cure winter squash at 25°C for 10 days to harden skin; store on single layers on slatted shelves with good airflow. Avoid chilling.

Zucchini.pres: Hydrocool to 8°C. Extremely sensitive to ethylene (causes rapid yellowing) and cold injury below 5°C (causes water-soaked pits).

Sponge Gourd.pres: Wrap individually in perforated paper wraps. Avoid temperatures below 10°C to prevent surface spotting and decay.

Ash Gourd.pres: Store intact fruits with their natural waxy coating on slatted wooden shelves. Do not wash or bruise outer skin.

Cauliflower.pres: Rapid hydrocooling or vacuum cooling. Retain jacket leaves to protect the white curd. Isolate from ethylene-producing apples.

Brussels Sprouts.pres: Forced-air cool to 0°C immediately. Package in vented film cartons; high ethylene sensitivity leads to yellowing and leaf loss.

Kohlrabi.pres: Trim tops to 2 cm; store in perforated master crates. Low temperature prevents rapid lignification of the inner edible bulb.

Kale.pres: Top-icing or ultrasonic humidification at near 100% RH prevents rapid moisture wilt; strictly exclude ethylene.

Celery.pres: Rapid hydrocooling or vacuum cooling. Pack in polyethylene-lined crates. Monitor stalks for petiole pithiness.

Asparagus.pres: Hydrocool to 2°C within 2 hours of harvest. Store spears upright with cut butts resting on damp moisture pads to prevent geotropic bending.

Artichoke.pres: Hydrocooling or room cooling to 0°C. Pack in film-lined cartons to stop bract wilting, feathering, and blackening.
Artichoke.fungus: Gray mold (Botrytis cinerea), Bacterial soft rot

Blueberry.pres: Forced-air pre-cooling to 0°C within 2 hours. Controlled atmosphere (3% O2, 10–12% CO2) suppresses decay without washing.

Raspberry.pres: Ultra-rapid cooling to 0°C within 1 hour. Elevated CO2 atmosphere (15–20%) halts gray mold. Handle in rigid clamshells.

Blackberry.pres: Pre-cool rapidly; protect berries from physical jarring and condensation which causes juice leakage (red cell reversion).

Cherry.pres: Hydrocooling with food-grade sanitizing wash. Modified atmosphere packaging liners (5% O2, 10% CO2) keep green stems fresh.

Plum.pres: Forced-air pre-cooling. Avoid holding at 2–7°C (internal breakdown / flesh translucency zone).

Peach.pres: Hydrocooling; avoid temperature holding between 2–8°C which induces mealiness, flesh browning, and woolly texture.

Pecan.pres: Dry in-shell to 4.5% kernel moisture. Store in sealed rooms with nitrogen flush or freezing to stop oil oxidation.

Macadamia.pres: De-husk immediately; dry slowly to 1.5% moisture; pack in nitrogen-flushed heavy foil vacuum barrier bags.
Macadamia.insects: Macadamia Nut Borer, Tropical Nut Borer

Hazelnut.pres: Dry to 6% moisture in forced-air dryers at 35°C; store in bulk totes with dehumidifiers away from off-odors.

Coffee.pres: Grade green beans to 10.5–11.5% moisture; package in multi-layer hermetic GrainPro liners to preserve cupping profile.
Coffee.fungus: Aspergillus ochraceus (Ochratoxin A danger if wet)

Tea.pres: Pack in airtight moisture-barrier foil-lined multi-wall paper sacks; isolate strictly from spices and high humidity.
Tea.fungus: Aspergillus mold if moisture rises above 7%

Cocoa.pres: Store dried fermented beans (moisture 6.5–7.5%) in jute bags on pallets 15 cm above ground and 50 cm away from walls.

Tobacco.pres: Condition cured leaves to 12–14% moisture; pack in wooden hogsheads or cardboard cases for fermentation aging.

Rubber.pres: Hang smoked sheets on timber racks in dark, ventilated sheds. Strictly protect from copper, UV light, and heat.
Rubber.fungus: Surface mold, Mildew in damp air

Turmeric.pres: Boil fresh fingers, sun-dry to 10% moisture, and polish. Store in dark airtight containers to prevent curcumin photo-oxidation.

Ginger.pres: Fresh ginger chills below 12°C. Dry sonth ginger should be sun-dried to 9% moisture and sealed in polythene bags.

Cardamom.pres: Cure green capsules in drying kilns at 45–50°C; pack in black polythene-lined wooden boxes to retain chlorophyll and cineole aroma.

Black Pepper.pres: Sun dry harvested berries until moisture drops below 11%; store in multi-wall paper bags with plastic barrier in aerated godowns.

Clove.pres: Dry buds in shade or solar kilns until stems snap cleanly; store in airtight tins or foil bags to halt eugenol oil evaporation.

Cinnamon.pres: Roll peeled bark into tight quills, shade dry to 11% moisture, and bind into compact bundles wrapped in moisture-proof paper.

Nutmeg.pres: Dry seed in shell for 6 weeks until kernels rattle; crack and remove shell; store in airtight tins in cool, dark rooms.

Vanilla.pres: Cured beans (25–30% moisture) bundled in parchment paper and kept in wooden conditioning boxes to develop vanillin aroma.

Saffron.pres: Rapid drying at 45°C immediately after flower harvesting; pack in airtight dark amber glass vials away from light and oxygen.

Coriander.pres: Dry fruits to 9% moisture; pack in polythene-lined jute sacks in well-ventilated dry warehouses to prevent seed darkening.

Cumin.pres: Clean and dry seeds to 8% moisture; pack in sealed tins or airtight laminated pouches to lock in cuminaldehyde essential oil.

Fennel.pres: Dry harvested umbels under shade to preserve vibrant green color; store in moisture-proof containers away from light.

Fenugreek.pres: Sun dry seeds to 9% moisture; store in galvanized drums or moisture-proof bags; hard seed coat offers natural pest resistance.

Apple.pres: Controlled Atmosphere (1.5% O2, 1.0% CO2) with rapid pre-cooling. Ethylene scrubbing extends storage life up to 10 months.

Banana.pres: Store mature green fruit at 13.5°C; do not store below 13°C (severe peel chilling injury). Ripen with ethylene in ripening rooms.

Orange.pres: Wash, wax with food-grade fungicidal wax, and store in well-ventilated plastic crates. Avoid stack pressure.

Mango.pres: Hot water dip treatment (48°C for 5 min) against anthracnose; store at 12–13°C to prevent chilling injury.
Mango.insects: Mango Seed Weevil, Oriental Fruit Fly

Grapes.pres: Rapid forced-air pre-cooling; pack with SO2 generator sheets in vented cartons to suppress Botrytis gray mold.

Potato.pres: Cure at 15°C for 2 weeks. Store in completely dark, ventilated cold storage; treat with CIPC sprout suppressant if table stock.
Potato.type: Darkened Cold Storage with Sprout Suppression

Tomato.pres: Store mature green fruit at 13–15°C. Never store below 10°C (causes chilling injury, uneven ripening, and watery breakdown).
Tomato.fungus: Alternaria rot, Early blight, Late blight

Onion.pres: Thorough field curing until necks are paper-dry; store in slatted wooden crates or mesh bags with high forced ventilation.
Onion.fungus: Neck rot (Botrytis allii), Black mold (Aspergillus niger)

Garlic.pres: Cure bulbs for 3 weeks; keep relative humidity low (<70%) to prevent root emergence and mold development.

Soybean.pres: Clean and screen broken splits; forced aeration to maintain uniform cool temperature; monitor for hot spots to prevent free fatty acid (FFA) increase and oil rancidity.
Soybean.fungus: Diaporthe phaseolorum (Pod & stem blight), Aspergillus flavus
Soybean.insects: Bean Weevil, Sawtoothed Grain Beetle, Indian Meal Moth

Chickpea.pres: Hermetic grain bins or triple-layer bags; keep moisture under 10% to prevent pulse beetle outbreaks.

Lentil.pres: Thoroughly dry to 10% moisture; store in clean airtight silos away from direct heat and moisture.

Groundnut.pres: Store in-shell at <7% kernel moisture. Maintain low temperature to avoid Aspergillus flavus and carcinogenic aflatoxin synthesis.
Groundnut.insects: Groundnut Borer (Caryedon serratus), Red Flour Beetle

Sunflower.pres: Dry seed to 8% moisture. Forced aeration prevents hot spots and rapid rancidity of high-oil seeds.
Sunflower.insects: Sunflower Moth larvae, Confused Flour Beetle

Papaya.pres: Hold at 10–12°C to slow ripening without chilling injury. Ethylene scrubbing in transit extends marketability.

Pomegranate.pres: Pre-cooling to 5°C. Package in plastic liner bags; keep above 5°C to avoid chilling husk scald.

Watermelon.pres: Well-ventilated ambient/cool warehouse. Store single or double-stacked; below 10°C chilling causes rind pitting.
Watermelon.fungus: Gummy stem blight, Fusarium fruit rot

Muskmelon.pres: Rapid forced-air or hydrocooling to 3°C within hours of picking. High humidity prevents rind wrinkling.

Cabbage.pres: Room cooling or forced air. Retain 2–3 wrapper leaves. Strictly isolate from apples and bananas (ethylene).

Carrot.pres: Hydrocooling to 1°C. Remove tops completely. Isolate from ethylene which synthesizes isocoumarin (bitter taste).

Almond.pres: Dry kernels to <6% moisture. Store in moisture-proof bins with insect-resistant seals and fumigation.

Walnut.pres: Dry immediately to 4% moisture. Cold storage prevents polyunsaturated fatty acid oxidation and bitter rancidity.
Walnut.insects: Walnut Husk Fly, Indian Meal Moth

Cashew.pres: Dry in-shell to 8% moisture. Kernel export in Vita-Pack vacuum-sealed nitrogen-flushed tins.

Sponge Guard.pres: Wrap individually in perforated paper wraps. Avoid temperatures below 10°C to prevent surface spotting and decay.

Aspargus.pres: Hydrocool to 2°C within 2 hours of harvest. Store spears upright with cut butts resting on damp moisture pads to prevent geotropic bending.

Chili.pres: For dry chillies: sun dry to <10% moisture; store in polythene-lined gunny bags in darkness to preserve bright red carotenoids.

Pigeon pea.pres: Sun dry to 9–10% moisture. Store in hermetic multi-layer PICS bags or sealed galvanized bins to suffocate pulse beetles.

Cow pea.pres: Solar heating on black plastic sheets before bagging to destroy internal bruchid larvae; seal in airtight hermetic bags.

Leek.pres: Rapid hydrocooling or forced-air cooling to 0°C. Store upright or in perforated film-lined crates. Highly sensitive to ethylene which triggers leaf yellowing and elongation.
Leek.fungus: Purple blotch (Alternaria porri), White tip (Phytophthora porri), Bacterial soft rot

Taro.pres: Cure corms at 30°C and 90% RH for 5 days after harvest to heal harvesting abrasions. Store in slatted wooden crates with steady cross-ventilation. Do NOT store below 10°C.
Taro.fungus: Taro leaf blight residual, Pythium soft rot, Fusarium corm dry rot

Canola.pres: Clean thoroughly to remove green dockage and weed seeds; aerate grain mass continuously in early storage to prevent moisture migration and heat-induced rancidity.
Canola.insects: Red flour beetle, Sawtoothed grain beetle

Soyabean.pres: Clean and screen broken splits; forced aeration to maintain uniform cool temperature; monitor for hot spots to prevent free fatty acid (FFA) increase and oil rancidity.
Soyabean.fungus: Diaporthe phaseolorum (Pod & stem blight), Aspergillus flavus
Soyabean.insects: Bean Weevil, Sawtoothed Grain Beetle, Indian Meal Moth
